48.0.0.en: 1 “Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah, which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness. 2 For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; The LORD of hosts is his name. 3 I have declared the former things from the beginning; and they went forth out of my mouth, and I shewed them; I did them suddenly, and they came to pass. 4 Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass; 5 I have even from the beginning declared it to thee; before it came to pass I shewed it thee: lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them. 6 Thou hast heard, see all this; and will not ye declare it? I have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them. 7 They are created now, and not from the beginning; even before the day when thou heardest them not; lest thou shouldest say, Behold, I knew them. 8 Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not; yea, from that time that thine ear was not opened: for I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.”

48.0.1.en: In the previous chapter God exposed Babylon, the virgin, the lady of kingdoms, who was swept away into a life of revelry with haughtiness and violence, and so collapsed completely. Now, before announcing the departure of His people or their release from captivity, He speaks in a fatherly rebuke, frank, revealing their weaknesses and sins and also His purposes in allowing their captivity, so that they might not return to their sins again.

48.0.2.en: Perhaps the most dangerous sin facing believers who have spiritual knowledge is hypocrisy together with formalism in worship. God does not want to humiliate them, but to raise them to a lofty position, and He gave them spiritual possibilities for life with Him, the most important of which are:

48.0.3.en: a. He called them “Israel” [1], as they are His chosen people.

48.0.4.en: b. A royal people, “come forth out of the waters of Judah” [1].

48.0.5.en: c. The name of God was called upon them: “which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel,” but they do this “not in truth, nor in righteousness” [1], although they realize that He is the one true God whom they worship, but in formalism and literalism without spirit.

48.1.0.en: d. They enjoyed the city of Jerusalem [2] as the holy city of God, which contains His temple.

48.1.1.en: e. “[They] stay themselves upon the God of Israel” [2]: they boast in His promises, confess His covenant and lean upon Him (Mic 3:11)..

48.2.0.en: f. They enjoyed the divine prophecies, for God used to tell them of the things to come, that is, of the things that were about to happen [3]. The secret of giving these prophecies was to establish them in faith in Him and in believing His words and promises. He knew that they were hard of heart, their necks iron and their brows brass, so that it was difficult for them to believe the prophetic words; therefore He gave them prophecies that were fulfilled in the near future so that they might believe the prophecies, and also to distinguish between God and the idols [5].

48.3.0.en: With all that God gave His people of these possibilities, they lived in formalism of worship with a Pharisaic spirit full of hypocrisy; they also mixed the worship of God with idols, and ignored the prophetic words and despised them and did not understand their mysteries. Therefore He rebukes them, saying: “Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not; yea, from that time that thine ear was not opened: for I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb” [8].

48.3.1.en: The prophet Isaiah was occupied with speaking of spiritual insight and the holy inner ear, for his talk about the Savior seemed to many in his time, indeed to the majority, almost impossible.

48.3.2.en: The Savior has come, and yet many reject Him in spite of the fulfillment of the prophecies that came in the Old Testament in His person and through His saving works; therefore the world still needs true insight and the holy ear. Even those who have believed in Him and received Him need this, to enjoy deeper mysteries and to perceive the hidden inner heavenly glories.

48.3.3.en: We all need the Lord of glory to accompany us and speak with us so as to sanctify our depths, so that we may say with the two disciples of Emmaus: “Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” (Lk 24:32).

48.3.4.en: * My God... You are my light, open my eyes that they may behold Your divine splendor, so that I may walk in my way without stumbling in the snares of the enemy.

48.3.5.en: * You are the light who enlightened the mind of Jacob, so he revealed to his children the various matters.

48.4.0.en: 9 “For my name’s sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off. 10 Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction. 11 For mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will I do it: for how should my name be polluted? and I will not give my glory unto another. 12 Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last. 13 Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together. 14 All ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things? The LORD hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans. 15 I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him: I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous. 16 Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me. 17 Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go. 18 O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea: 19 Thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me.”

48.4.1.en: God presents to His people the reasons for allowing their captivity:

48.4.2.en: a. “For my name’s sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off” [9]... In other words, this people should have perished completely and been cut off, but God in His jealousy for His name and glory gave them over to discipline, that perhaps they might return to Him and not perish. It is as though the captivity were a “gift,” being a divine discipline offered to the beloved, despite their unworthiness of this fatherly disciplinary love.

48.4.3.en: This is a wonderful spiritual view of discipline, through which the believer realizes that he is not worthy of this discipline, as it is a sign of fatherly love. The Apostle says: “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons” (Heb 12:6-7).

48.4.4.en: * If the absence of discipline is a sign peculiar to bastards (Heb 12:8), then it is fitting for us to rejoice in discipline as a sign of the legitimacy of our sonship!

48.4.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * A father does not discipline his son if he does not love him, and a teacher does not correct his pupil unless he sees in him signs of obtaining the promise. When a physician withdraws his care from a patient, this is a sign that he despairs of his recovery.

48.4.6.en: St. Jerome * “Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes” (Ps 89:32).

48.4.7.en: It is mercy (of God) not only to call them but also to discipline them and scourge them. Let your father’s hand be upon you; if you are a good son, do not murmur at discipline... Let him discipline him as long as he has not taken away his mercy from him; let him strike him when he sins as long as he does not prevent him from inheriting.

48.4.8.en: If you rightly understand your father’s promises, do not fear his scourgings, but fear lest you do not inherit...

48.4.9.en: May the pious children not say: “If You come to us with a rod, do not come at all. For it is better to learn by the Father’s rod than to perish by the thief’s care for you.

48.4.10.en: * The Lord, the Preserver of the little ones (Ps 116:6), scourges those whom, when they become mature, He seeks to be (His) heirs...

48.4.11.en: He helped me when I was in distress, for the pain that the physician causes with his scalpel is not for punishment but for honor.

48.5.0.en: St. Augustine b. For purification: “Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction” [10]. We are the silver and gold of the Lord; He cares for refining us in the furnaces of toil and pain.

48.5.1.en: * Blessed is the man who is disciplined in this life twice, for the Lord does not punish for anything twice (Nah 1:9) LXX.

48.6.0.en: St. Jerome c. God, who allows discipline to purify us, lifts it from us when He accomplishes His aim. He has called the heavens and the earth, that all creation may gather and see the marvelous salvation of God. He loved Cyrus to accomplish His aim, and that his arm be on the Chaldeans [14].

48.7.0.en: What Cyrus accomplishes is not of his own, but from God, the Savior of His people: “I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him: I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous” [15]... “from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me” [6].

48.7.1.en: Cyrus was sent by the Lord and by the Holy Spirit of God, as a symbol of the Lord Christ, who came of His own will and at the same time was sent by the Father and the Holy Spirit... How?

48.7.2.en: Here is the unity of the work of the Holy Trinity; the Holy Trinity, as inseparable hypostases of one divine essence, works for the salvation of humanity.

48.7.3.en: The Father loves humanity, and in His love He sent His Word, who is not separated from Him, reckoning the sacrifice of Christ a gift on the part of the Father, as the Lord Christ Himself said: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life” (Jn 3:16). The Father, the Lover of mankind, sent His Son as a sacrifice of love.

48.7.4.en: The Son on His part offered Himself to be given in obedience to the Father, and also of His full will, for the Apostle says: “who loved me, and gave himself for me” (Gal 2:20).

48.7.5.en: As for the Holy Spirit, He did not stand in a passive role but had His positive role in the whole work of salvation; by Him the divine Incarnation was accomplished in the womb of the Virgin (Lk 1:35), and it is He who led Jesus up to be tempted, and He who bears witness to the Lord Christ (Jn 15:26).

48.8.0.en: g. To practice obedience to God, for the captivity did not happen by chance nor by fate and destiny, but is the natural fruit of disobedience; without it they would not have fallen into captivity. Therefore they ought, on their return, to practice obedience, so that they may enjoy the righteousness of God and His good things. “O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea: Thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me” [18-19].

48.8.1.en: Had they obeyed God, not only would they not have fallen into the Babylonian captivity, but the peace of God would have overflowed like a wide, deep and ever-flowing river, watering many.

48.9.0.en: 20 “Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth; say ye, The LORD hath redeemed his servant Jacob. 21 And they thirsted not when he led them through the deserts: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them: he clave the rock also, and the waters gushed out. 22 There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked.”

48.9.1.en: God presents a call to depart: “Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans” [20].

48.9.2.en: Although God sent Cyrus for their deliverance, He does not compel them to depart against their will, but calls them and urges them to do so... And indeed 40,000 persons went out under Zerubbabel (Neh 7:66-67).

48.9.3.en: It is a continual call for us to depart, under the leadership of our Savior, from every place of stumbling, so that we may be freed by the Spirit of God from its yoke, as Lot and his family were called to leave Sodom and Gomorrah.

48.9.4.en: Fleeing from evil is not weakness nor passivity, but a bold act in which man, by the Spirit of God, declares his victory over his depths that long for or find pleasant the places of stumbling.

48.9.5.en: This call is accompanied by joy and rejoicing in the saving work of God: “with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this” [20].

48.10.0.en: As the prophet Isaiah looks at the release from captivity as a second exodus resembling the people’s departure from the bondage of Pharaoh by the hand of Moses, when He brought forth water for them from the rock in the wilderness that they might not thirst, so in this new exodus they enjoy the same gift: “And they thirsted not when he led them through the deserts: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them: he clave the rock also, and the waters gushed out” [21]. This was fulfilled when the salvation of the Lord Christ was joined with the gift of the Holy Spirit on the feast of Pentecost, as a spring of living water that overflowed in the Church of Christ.

48.11.0.en: Finally, this salvation is optional; whoever does not accept it is deprived of the surpassing peace of God, for it is said: “There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked” [22].

48.11.1.en: * It is said to us: “I will cause the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness to cease from their mouths” (Jer 7:34). Yes, for the feasts of the wicked are woes.

48.11.2.en: * When the ungrateful withdraw from prayer and thanksgiving, they deprive themselves of the fruit of joy.

48.11.3.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic The Septuagint reads: “There is no joy, saith the Lord, to the wicked.” St. Augustine distinguished between the temporary joy of the wicked, bound to temporal things and passing away with them, and the righteous, who rejoice even in their chains. The martyr Crispina rejoiced when she was bound and when she was led away to trial, as when she was imprisoned and when the sentence was passed against her... Her joy was before the angels, as the psalmist says: “Before the angels I will sing praise unto thee” (Ps 138:1).

49.0.s.en: 1. The humility and glorification of the Savior:

49.0.0.en: 1 “Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, ye people, from far; The LORD hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. 2 And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; 3 And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified. 4 Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the LORD, and my work with my God. 5 And now, saith the LORD that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the LORD, and my God shall be my strength. 6 And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth. 7 Thus saith the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the LORD that is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, and he shall choose thee.”

49.0.1.en: In the previous chapter the address was directed to the house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel (Isa 48:1), but the address here is directed to the Gentiles, for He says: “Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, ye people, from far” [1]. The Gentiles were called “the isles of the Gentiles” (Gen 10:5), since they looked to the islands of the Mediterranean as the distant western regions, foreign to Israel; and He called the Gentiles “from far” because they had not entered into fellowship with Israel.

49.0.2.en: The Lord Christ the Savior speaks to the Gentiles, declaring the following:

49.0.3.en: a. Called from the womb: “The LORD hath called me from the womb” [1]. Some scholars think that the speaker here is in the name of Israel, since God chose His people before they existed, while they were in the loins of Abraham and in the womb of Sarah; and some thought it was Cyrus, whom God chose to accomplish his mission before he existed; but it is clear that the address here is in the name of the Lord Christ, the incarnate Word of God; for the archangel Gabriel preached to the Virgin His birth before she conceived Him, and He was called Jesus because He saves His people from their sins (Mt 1:21); therefore it is said, “from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name” [1].

49.1.0.en: b. Possessing authority: “And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword” [2]. And it is said of the Lord Christ:

49.1.1.en: “out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword” (Rev 1:16), and it is said of Him that He spoke as one having authority, and not as the scribes and Pharisees (Mt 7:29). He entered the battle against the enemy of good, the devil, with His word, which is like a twoedged sword (Heb 4:12).

49.1.2.en: c. The hiding of the mystery of Christ, His saving Gospel work and His call of the Gentiles to faith, behind the shadows of the Mosaic Law and the prophecies, for He says, “in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me” [2]. Perhaps by this saying He also meant what happened in His childhood, when Herod rose against Him and wanted to kill Him, so the Father sent an angel to Joseph commanding him to flee to Egypt. The Word became flesh, the Son of God became the Son of man; therefore in His humility He walked in our way as one of us, guarded by the Father with His protection as in the shadow of His hand, though He is able to command nature to destroy Herod and all who oppose Him.

49.1.3.en: “And made me a polished shaft (that does not rust); in his quiver hath he hid me” [2]. As the Word of God, He is an arrow that does not rust; He was hidden behind the shadows and symbols until the fullness of time came, and He declared Himself through the Cross as an arrow aimed against the devil and his hosts, stripping them of their authority and making a public show of them, triumphing over them (Col 2:15). He is the arrow that kills evil, and the giver of the wounds of divine love to the believing souls who cry out, “I am sick with love” (Song 2:5; 5:8).

49.1.4.en: * Holy Scripture teaches us that God is love (1 Jn 4:8); He aimed His only-begotten Son, “the chosen arrow” [2], toward the chosen, planting its threefold point in the spirit of life.

49.1.5.en: The head of the arrow is faith, which joins the one who shoots the arrow (Christ) with those who are struck by it, as though the soul were raised by divine ascents, and sees within itself the arrow of sweet love wounding it, adorned with the wounds....

49.1.6.en: It is a good wound, and a sweet pain, by which “Life” pierces the soul.

49.1.7.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * Can anyone see the many wounds of divine love like those in the Song of Songs, she who complains that she is wounded: “I am wounded with love” (Song 2:5)?! And can he see the arrow that wounds many souls with the love of God except in Him who said: “He made me like a chosen spear”?!

49.1.8.en: * If anyone was ever inflamed with sincere love for the Word of God, if anyone received the sweet wounds of this “chosen arrow,” as the prophet calls it, if anyone was wounded by the spear of His knowledge, worthy of all love, so that he yearns and longs for Him night and day, and cannot speak except of Him, nor listen except to Him, nor think except of Him, nor incline to any desire or hope for anything else, when the matter becomes so, the soul rightly says: “I am wounded with love.” She receives her wound from the One of whom it was said: “He made me a chosen arrow, and in His quiver He hides me” [2].

49.1.9.en: It is fitting for God to strike our souls with such a wound, to wound them with such arrows and spears, to strike them with such healing wounds.

49.1.10.en: Origen * The words of the Lord are arrows that kindle love, not pain... Therefore we ought to understand “thine arrows stick fast in me” (Ps 38:2) thus: Your words have stuck fast in my heart.

49.1.11.en: * May the unhealthy be wounded, for when they are rightly wounded they become healthy. Let these, having become dwellers in the Church, the Body of Christ, say with the Church: “I am wounded with love” (Song 2:5) LXX.

49.2.0.en: St. Augustine d. By the Cross the Son submitted in obedience to the Father; He became a servant for our sake that the Father might be glorified in Him, and that He might also be glorified in the weakness of the Cross. “And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified. Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the LORD, and my work with my God” [4].

49.2.1.en: Some ask: Who is His servant Israel? He is the Lord Christ, who came from the Jews, and accepted servitude by His own will although He is equal to the Father in essence (Phil 2:7). He came as a servant to raise the servants in Him to sonship to God; by this He glorified the Father and was glorified Himself through weakness, for the Apostle says: “And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father” (Phil 2:8-11).

49.2.2.en: In the moments of suffering, when the Lord of glory appeared as in weakness, He said: “I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do. And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was” (Jn 17:4-5).

49.2.3.en: If the Cross is shame and weakness outwardly, yet it is glory inwardly. Origen says: [We do not hesitate to say that the goodness of Christ appears in a greater way and with the divine light... for “he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” (Phil 2:6-8)].

49.2.4.en: The Cross is also glory because it reconciled the Father with mankind, and opened before us the door of Paradise that we may share the Lord’s glory and live with Him praising Him with the heavenly ones.

49.2.5.en: Some see that what is said here also concerns the Church hidden in the Savior, as the new Israel, which glorifies God through accepting fellowship in the sufferings and crucifixion with her Christ and so enjoys the power of His resurrection and its joy; therefore she deserved to hear the divine voice: “Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” But she, in her sufferings, says: “I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the LORD, and my work with my God” [4].

49.2.6.en: e. The success of the mission of the Lord Christ in bringing the Gentiles into the faith: if the Lord appeared on the Cross in weakness until all forsook Him, for He came unto His own, and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11), and became wounded in the house of His friends (Zech 13:6), so He said: “I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain” [4]; this is the outward appearance of the Cross, but its inward work is declared by the Father with power, saying to the Crucified One: “It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth” [6]. It is as though He were saying to the crucified Son: Your work of redemption cannot have its fruit confined within the limits of a particular people, but extends to the end of the earth, so that you are a light to the Gentiles and the mystery of divine salvation for all mankind.

49.2.7.en: When the elder Simeon carried the Child Jesus he said: “For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel” (Lk 2:30-31). As Paul and Barnabas said: “For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth” (Acts 13:46-47). Origen says: [Had He not become a servant He would not have raised up the tribes of Jacob nor changed the heart of scattered Israel, and would not have become a light to the Gentiles for the salvation of the end of the earth].

49.2.8.en: Our Christ came as a light to the peoples and the Gentiles; the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world (Jn 1:9), calling us out of darkness into light (1 Pet 2:9) that we may walk in the light and become children of light and children of the day (1 Thess 5:5), and even become the light of the world (Mt 5:14). By this the saying of the prophet Isaiah is fulfilled: [The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God oil; thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon be diminished: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light] (Isa 60:19-20). The Savior, the light of the Gentiles, shines upon the soul as His bride, so she perceives the secrets of wisdom (Job 11:6).

49.2.9.en: * My Lord and my God... O light of my soul! Never cease to illumine my steps...!

49.2.10.en: My God... You are my hope... without Your light, by which we behold everything, it is difficult for us to discover the maneuvers of Satan and his wiles.

49.2.11.en: * You are the Word who said: “Let there be light,” and there was light. Say this word now also, that my eyes may be enlightened by the true light, and I may distinguish it from other light; for without You how can I distinguish light from darkness, and darkness from light?!

49.3.0.en: St. Augustine The Jews insulted Him and denied Him, seeking His crucifixion, and the pagan peoples received Him, submitted to Him by faith and accepted His work. Therefore the Lord was called “him whom man despiseth,” “him whom the nation abhorreth,” “a servant of rulers,” for the wicked ruled over Him and hated Him and insulted Him; and at the same time it is said, “Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” [7]. For kings rise from their thrones in His presence, and princes worship Him in adoration.

49.4.0.en: 8 “Thus saith the LORD, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages; 9 That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves. They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places. 10 They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them. 11 And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted. 12 Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim. 13 Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.”

49.4.1.en: Before us is a wonderful divine address that reveals the mystery of our salvation in Jesus Christ our inexpressible Lord; for in Christ the Savior we receive the following:

49.4.2.en: a. God’s answering us; the time has come for the Father to hear us through His beloved Son crucified as a sacrifice of obedience to the Father and the object of His pleasure, so that the Father answers us in Him, giving Himself to us as Father, offering us His bosom as a place of eternal rest in which we settle. This is what He meant by His saying, “In an acceptable time have I heard thee” [8]. The time has come in which our acceptance with the Father is declared in His Son, accepted from eternity, so He answers us continually.

49.4.3.en: b. Through Christ Jesus our Savior, God Himself has become a help and helper to us: “and in a day of salvation have I helped thee” [8]. The Lord Himself took over the leading of the battle against the enemy of good that we may hide in Him and obtain in Him the victory and triumph. As the Apostle says: “Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place” (2 Cor 2:14). St. Augustine says: [This is the day in which the Intercessor became the chief cornerstone; let us rejoice and be glad in it].

49.4.4.en: It is fitting for us to distinguish between “the day of salvation” [8] or “the day of the Lord” and our own days; the day of the Lord is joyful and gives salvation, but our days in which we walk according to our desire are destructive and ruinous. St. Augustine says: [Rather I call my days (Ps 116:2) the days of my misery, the days of my death, the days according to Adam, full of toil and sweat, the days according to the old corruption. For he cries in another psalm: “I sink in deep mire” (Ps 69:2), “Behold, You have made my days old” (Ps 39:5); in these days of mine I call upon You (Ps 61:2). For my days are different from the days of my Lord].

49.5.0.en: c. By the Crucified One we have also become preserved in the Lord, for He says: “I will preserve thee” [9]. In the farewell prayer the Savior says: “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil... Sanctify them in thy truth” (Jn 17:15, 17).

49.5.1.en: d. The enjoyment of the Crucified One as a covenant with the Father: “and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages” [8]. God gave His new covenant not engraved on stones but recorded in blood in the body of the Son, the incarnate Word; through this covenant the Church does not enjoy the land of promise flowing with milk and honey, but inherits the earth, that is, the peoples who were desolate like the wildernesses, to establish from them a divine paradise and a heavenly kingdom. In the body of His humanity He reconciled the Father with humanity and established in every truly believing heart an inexpressible inheritance.

49.5.2.en: The characteristics of this new Kingdom, or inner inheritance, or Gospel life, the true Church, are:

49.5.3.en: First: Freedom; “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves” [9]. He broke the bars of Hades and gave us the freedom of the glory of the children of God, so that we live bearing authority over serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy (Lk 10:19), walking in the light, with no authority of darkness over us.

49.5.4.en: Our Savior gave us inner freedom, so that we are not enslaved to the enemy of good, nor to the lusts of the flesh, nor to the love of the world; but what is more important is that we are not enslaved to the ego, that we no longer shut ourselves up in the ego, but are crucified with our Savior Christ to declare the breadth of our heart, to bear in it the unlimited God, and that it may have room for every human being, even those who oppose us.

49.5.5.en: Through this inner freedom we accept willingly to submit to God as His servants, so we live free, with no authority of the enemy over our depths.

49.5.6.en: * Be a servant and free at the same time; be a servant by your submission to God, free, not enslaved to anything, neither to empty praise nor to any passion.

49.5.7.en: * Free yourself from the chains of sin, live in freedom, for Christ has made you free (Gal 5:1). Seek the freedom of the new world during your temporal life. Do not enslave yourself to the love of money nor to praise that comes from pleasing people.

49.5.8.en: * Do not set a rule for yourself lest you be enslaved to rules of your own making. Be free, a human being in a position that allows him to do what he wills.

49.5.9.en: * Free yourself from the yoke of the world by the freedom of the new life.

49.5.10.en: * Be free, free yourself from every ruinous bondage; for if you do not become free, do not be a worker for Christ, for the kingdom of the heavenly, free Jerusalem does not accept the children of bondage. The children of the free mother are themselves free (Rom 8:5), and are not enslaved to the world in anything.

49.5.11.en: * Do not bind yourself to an effort beyond your capacity, lest you enslave yourself to the need to please others.

49.5.12.en: Abba John the Syrian the Solitary Second: The enjoyment of a rich divine pasture, “They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places” [9]. What is this way but the Savior who called Himself “the Way” (Jn 14:6)? By Him we enter into fruitful high places to find all our needs, so we neither hunger nor thirst, nor does heat or sun smite us; in them are the springs of the Holy Spirit as living waters that water our depths and give us fruit [10].

49.6.0.en: Third: The enjoyment of a smoothed way that brings us into the divine embraces, “And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted” [11]. What are these mountains but the commandments of the Lord, which seem like lofty mountains difficult to climb, but by our union with Christ “the Way,” walking over the mountains becomes natural, and the commandment turns into delight and joy, not harsh commands and deprivation.

49.6.1.en: At the time when He makes the difficult commandment easy, as He turns His lofty mountains into a way in which we rejoice to pass, He says, “and my highways (my paths) shall be exalted,” meaning that the ease of the commandment does not mean our descending to lower things and being lenient with ourselves in accepting bodily pleasures and fulfilling temporal desires, but on the contrary He carries us by His paths upward to practice the heavenly, exalted life with gladness of heart and joy, as a life that is acceptable and joyful in the Lord.

49.7.0.en: Fourth: The opening of the doors of the Church before all the Gentiles from the east and west and north and south. “Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim” [12]. By those coming from afar He means the inhabitants of the Far East, and by the land of Sinim (Aswan) He means the south of Egypt, as representing those coming from the south.

49.8.0.en: Fifth: The enjoyment of the life of praise and joy as a life lived by the soul (the heavens) and practiced by the body (the earth) and expressed by the salvation of human energies (the mountains). Thus the heavens share with the earth and its mountains in singing to the Lord, “for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted” [13].

49.8.1.en: The secret of our joy is God’s comforts declared by the Holy Spirit in our depths through the merits of the precious Blood, for the Crucified One raised us from our misery and had compassion on us with His practical mercy.

49.8.2.en: This joy spreads over the whole Church extending here through the generations and also in heaven; therefore St. Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [We are not alone in our joy, for in heaven the whole “church of the firstborn” (Heb 12:23) rejoices with us... See, my friends, all creation keeps the feast with us, for the psalmist says: “Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD” (Ps 150:5), and that because of the destruction of the enemies of the Lord and because of our salvation].

49.8.3.en: Now we have seen how the Lord moved from speaking of Cyrus as the rescuer of the people of God from captivity to what is greater and more lasting, speaking of the Lord Christ as the Savior of all humanity, rescuing them from eternal captivity to grant them the blessings of His salvation by bringing them into His Kingdom, that is, the enjoyment of the new, joyful life of the Church in the Lord, as a paradisal life offered to all peoples and nations.

49.9.s.en: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

49.9.0.en: 14 “But Zion said, The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me. 15 Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee. 16 Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me. 17 Thy children shall make haste; thy destroyers and they that made thee waste shall go forth of thee. 18 Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to thee. As I live, saith the LORD, thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on thee, as a bride doth. 19 For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants, and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away. 20 The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell. 21 Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?”

49.9.1.en: The people of God did not expect to be taken captive, and when Israel, the northern kingdom, was taken captive, the kingdom of Judah thought that it would not be taken captive because it embraced the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, the city of God. But Judah was taken captive and Jerusalem collapsed with the temple, which they had defiled with idolatrous worship and abominations, as is recorded in Ezekiel and Jeremiah. The captives thought that it would perhaps be a few months and God would intervene to free them, but months passed and years upon years, so the people thought that God had forgotten them, and all felt isolation, deprivation and abandonment. This is what the prophet expressed here thus: “But Zion said, The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me” [14]. This feeling of isolation is a natural fruit suffered by most human beings, if not all of them, at some moments. For man in the time of trial feels himself alone, with no one to share his feelings and sensations and no one to touch his inner bitterness.

49.9.2.en: Psychologists complain of this disease, “the feeling of isolation,” as a disease that is almost universal, especially among adolescents, when they realize that those closest to them cannot understand the reality of their inner world and their hidden feelings.

49.9.3.en: The cure for this disease is the meeting with the Savior, who alone can enter into the depths and raise His banner as love, declaring by His Cross a unique personal friendship through which we enjoy a surpassing divine love and a union with God that time cannot and events cannot shatter. By the Cross God gathered humanity to Himself as a holy heavenly bride whom her heavenly Bridegroom does not forsake, instead of the feeling of abandonment.

49.9.4.en: And, wonderfully, the Savior Himself cried out on the Cross, saying: “Eloi, Eloi... why hast thou forsaken me?!” (Mk 15:34). It is as though, as the representative of humanity and in its stead, He declares our position as forsaken and deprived! By the Cross He became as one forsaken in order to remove from us the feeling of deprivation and abandonment and to return us to the divine embraces as a holy bride!

49.9.5.en: Now how does the Lord answer Zion’s feeling of deprivation?

49.10.0.en: “Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee” [15]. Without doubt motherhood is considered one of the highest degrees of human love, for the mother who carries her son or daughter as a fetus for months in her womb can hardly forget him after his birth. And yet some mothers have forgotten their sons and daughters, for some of them offered their children as human sacrifices, casting them into the fire amid the beating of drums as a kind of worship to the god Baal. And in some famines we hear of mothers who ate their children. And we still hear now of crimes of killing committed by some mothers against their children. And every day we also see mothers and fathers killing their children through the gloomy family atmosphere or family problems, especially separation and divorce. How many are the victims of divorce?! Fathers and mothers have had no mercy on the new generations, nor have they given them any account in their lives, but in selfishness they wish to achieve what they think is peace at the expense of the lives of their children and their spiritual and psychological peace and sometimes their social and material well-being also.

49.10.1.en: A mother may forget her infant, but God does not forget us!

49.10.2.en: * This care of God and His love, which the Lord shows by His goodness... He compares them to the heart of a mother full of tenderness and kindness, as He wants to express it by an example of human affection, for He found in His creation no better feelings of love with which to compare.

49.10.3.en: Abba Chaeremon * He not only cares for us, but loves us without limit, a holy burning love, an intense true love that cannot be broken or quenched...

49.10.4.en: * The prophet answers those who were once depressed and groaned, saying, “The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me,” saying: “Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?” It is as though he says: It is impossible for a mother to forget her infant, so much the more will the Lord not forget humanity. By this he does not mean to liken God’s love for us to the love of a mother for the fruit of her womb, but because a mother’s love surpasses every love, yet God’s love is surely greater than it. Therefore He says: “yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee, saith the Lord.” Consider how God’s love surpasses a mother’s love...?!

49.10.5.en: The Lord of the prophets and the Master of all affirms that His love surpasses the love of a father for his children, as light surpasses darkness and good surpasses evil... Listen to what He says: “Or what man of you, if his son ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?” (Mt 7:9-11). As good differs from evil, so the love of God is higher than the affections of parents...

49.10.6.en: There are other examples, such as the love of a lover for his beloved, yet this love will not equal God’s love (Ps 103:11)..

49.11.0.en: St. John Chrysostom “Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands” [16]. It was among the ancient Eastern customs that a person engraves the name of his beloved on his palm, as a sign that he will not forget her until death, and that all he does with his hands is on behalf of his beloved. The Lord engraved the name of His beloved Church on His palm with the nails, so that the marks of the wounds might remain a sign of eternal love! Indeed, He engraved the name of every member in her on His palm as a sign of His personal love for us by our names.

49.11.1.en: “Thy walls are continually before me” [16]; as though He says: I know that your walls have been broken down, I will not forget them, I will build them but at the appointed time, I will restore to you your strength and your fortification, and I will return your sons to My land and drive out the destroyers and wasters from it [17].

49.11.2.en: Who are these sons hastening to Zion but those who accept the faith, who come to the Church of the New Testament and enjoy its walls, which are not made by human hands; as for the destroyers and wasters, they are those who deny the faith, who are driven out of it.

49.12.0.en: “Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to thee. As I live, saith the LORD, thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on thee, as a bride doth” [18]. What a splendid picture of the Church of the New Testament! For instead of the city whose walls were broken down, whose people were driven out as captives, and which the destroyers and wasters entered, the Lord establishes the Church of the New Testament not merely as a fortified city to which her children return in haste and from which the wicked wasters are driven out, but she becomes a heavenly bride bearing a unique adornment, which is the gathering of her children in her as children of God, who have the freedom of inner glory. In the East a woman’s beauty was her children; she boasted in them as her glory and as her continual wedding garment; so the Church takes pride in her children glorified in her, like a precious bridal girdle with which she girds herself.

49.12.1.en: She becomes a fruitful bride, a fertile mother, whose spiritual children multiply until it seems that the earth has become too narrow for them and there is no place for the wasters to dwell with them.

49.13.0.en: The enemy does not stand silent but wants to enter and ruin her children, he who earlier bereaved her by destroying the faith of some, for he says to her: “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell” [20]. But she sees the wonderful hand of God working in her despite the continual opposition of the enemy, and repeats in her heart, saying: “Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?” [21]. It is the surpassing grace of God that brings forth food out of the eater and sweetness out of the strong! It is His rich grace that raises up in us abundant fruit, not of ourselves, but a free gift of God to His believers who walk by the Spirit.
